class.name: SteamAudioPlayer
class.brief_description: This player's transform is used as the audio source transform in the SteamAudio simulation.

method.name: stop_ringing_out
method.description: Ends the source and lets its reverb decay, instead of cutting both at once the way [method AudioStreamPlayer3D.stop] does. The player reports itself as playing until the effects have nothing left.

method.name: is_path_active
method.description: Whether the simulation is currently carrying this source to the listener along a path. False wherever there is line of sight, or no route at all.

method.name: get_path_level
method.description: How much energy the current path carries, as the magnitude of its ambisonic coefficients. Zero when there is no route.

method.name: play_stream
method.description: Plays the given stream starting at from_offset, at the defined volume and pitch scale. [b]A very important note[/b]: play_stream is what you want to use if you'd like to change a SteamAudioPlayer's stream at runtime. Do not try to set the player's stream directly through set_stream, as that will disable all SteamAudio effects for that player. At runtime, the stream you've configured will be replaced with a [SteamAudioStream]. This stream has an inner stream which corresponds to what you configured in the scene.

members.member: Whether Steam Audio's distance attenuation is enabled. On by default: a 3D source that does not get quieter with distance is rarely what anyone wants. Steam Audio's curve replaces Godot's rather than stacking with it, so enabling this disables the node's own [code]attenuation_model[/code]; turn it off to use Godot's curve instead.

The maximum distance from the listener at which reflection simulation is run for this audio source. Keep in mind that this does not disable reflection if it has already been simulated, it just doesn't update the effect.

See [url=https://valvesoftware.github.io/steam-audio/doc/capi/simulation.html#_CPPv4N27IPLDistanceAttenuationModel11minDistanceE]IPLDistanceAttenuationModel.minDistance[/url], and note the distance attenuation type in godot-steam-audio is always [code]IPL_DISTANCEATTENUATIONTYPE_INVERSEDISTANCE[/code].
Whether SteamAudio occlusion and transmission is enabled.

Take reflections from the reverb baked into a [SteamAudioProbeBatch] instead of simulating them. Much cheaper, but it does not follow moving geometry. Needs [member reflection] on and a batch baked with [member SteamAudioProbeBatch.reverb_bake]. Baked reverb describes the room the [i]listener[/i] is in, not the room the source is in, so it is sent in at the gain the source's direct path has: a source you cannot hear does not excite it. Expect it to sound like the space around you rather than the space around the source.

Play back the route sound takes around corners, using the paths baked into a [SteamAudioProbeBatch]. This is what makes an occluded source audible through a doorway instead of only muffled through the wall. On by default, and free until a probe batch with baked pathing exists: with no probes the simulator skips the source entirely. Occlusion alone has no diffraction model, so without this a source behind cover drops to whatever leaks through the material, and the level swings as the listener moves or turns.
Ambisonic order used to place the paths in space. Clamped to [member SteamAudioConfig.max_ambisonics_order].

Re-check baked paths against the current scene, so a door that closes cuts the path it was baked through and a different route is used when one exists. Costs a path search per source on the frames where a baked path is blocked; turn it off for a level with no moving geometry.
Probe radius used when re-checking visibility. Match the value the batch was baked with.
Probes further apart than this are not considered mutually visible when re-checking.
Fraction of rays that must get through for two probes to count as mutually visible when re-checking.
